q: Who designed the old Iloilo City Hall (now UP Visayas)?
n: Juan Arellano designed the old Iloilo City Hall (1936), now the UP Visayas Iloilo City campus building. Source: NHCP; UP Visayas history.

q: Who designed the Capitol Theater on Escolta?
n: Juan Nakpil designed the Art Deco Capitol Theater on Escolta (1935), with bas-reliefs by Francesco Riccardo Monti. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Nakpil); Escolta heritage records.

q: Which building, designed by Juan F. Nakpil, features a low podium and a 60-meter slab tower clad in a curtain wall?
n: Juan F. Nakpil designed the SSS Building in Quezon City, a low podium with a tall curtain-walled slab tower. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Juan F. Nakpil).

q: Which school was designed by Antonio Toledo?
o: University of the Philippines, P. Faura
n: Antonio Toledo designed buildings for the University of the Philippines on Padre Faura, Manila, during the American period, alongside his other government works. Source: Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: Who designed the Paco Railroad Station?
n: William E. Parsons, Consulting Architect of the Insular Government, designed the Paco Railroad Station (1915). Source: NHCP; Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: Who designed the Meralco Building in Ortigas?
n: José María Zaragoza designed the Meralco Building on Ortigas Avenue, Pasig (1968). Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Zaragoza).

q: Which pioneer of modern Philippine architecture, named National Artist in 1976, designed Far Eastern University?
n: Pablo S. Antonio, National Artist for Architecture in 1976, designed the Art Deco buildings of Far Eastern University. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Pablo Antonio).

q: Who was UP's first University Architect, designer of several UP Diliman buildings and the Insular Life Building?
n: Cesar Concio was UP's first University Architect, designing several UP Diliman buildings, as well as the Insular Life Building. Source: UP Diliman history; Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: Who was the architect of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas?
n: Gabriel Formoso designed the Central Bank of the Philippines (Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas) complex in Manila. Source: Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino; BSP history.

q: Which Filipino architect, artist and interior designer is known for concrete, floating volumes and simple forms?
n: Leandro Locsin, architect, artist and interior designer, is known for concrete, floating volumes and simple forms. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Locsin).

q: Who designed the Folk Arts Theater, the CCP and PHILCITE?
n: Leandro Locsin designed the CCP Theater of Performing Arts (1969), the Folk Arts Theater (1974) and PHILCITE (1976), all on the CCP Complex. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Locsin); Cultural Center of the Philippines.

q: Which architect insisted architecture must respond to local conditions and designed the Coconut Palace in 1978?
n: Francisco Mañosa insisted architecture must respond to local climate and culture. He designed the Coconut Palace (Tahanang Pilipino) in 1978. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Mañosa).

q: Who pioneered landscape architecture in the Philippines?
n: Ildefonso P. Santos Jr. pioneered landscape architecture in the Philippines and was proclaimed National Artist for Architecture in 2006. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Santos).

q: Who is the architect of the Galaxy Theater?
n: The Galaxy Theater is listed among Pablo S. Antonio's works. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Pablo Antonio).

q: Who is the architect of SM Megamall in Mandaluyong and Harrison Plaza Shopping Center?
n: Antonio Sindiong designed SM Megamall in Mandaluyong and the Harrison Plaza Shopping Center in Manila. Source: Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino; SM Prime project records.

q: Who was the architect of Quiapo Church before its restoration in 1988?
n: Juan Nakpil rebuilt Quiapo Church in 1933 after a fire. It was later expanded in 1984–88 under José María Zaragoza. Source: NCCA (Nakpil); Quiapo Church (Minor Basilica of the Black Nazarene) history.

q: In 1941, who founded the Philippine College of Design with Andrés Luna de San Pedro, Juan Arellano and Pablo Antonio?
n: In 1941 Juan Nakpil, with Andrés Luna de San Pedro, Juan Arellano and Pablo Antonio, founded the Philippine College of Design. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Nakpil).

q: Which is a project of Felipe Mendoza?
n: Felipe Mendoza designed the Batasang Pambansa Complex in Quezon City (1978). Source: UAP Likha Award records; House of Representatives history.

q: Antonio Toledo designed Manila City Hall during the American Period. Which of these is NOT his work?
n: Antonio Toledo designed Manila City Hall, the Legislative Building (completed with Arellano), the Department of Tourism (Agriculture and Commerce) Building and the Leyte Provincial Capitol. Muntinlupa City Hall is not his work. Source: NHCP; Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: To whom is the design of San Sebastian Church, the first all-steel church in Asia, popularly (though inaccurately) attributed?
n: San Sebastián Church is popularly attributed to Gustave Eiffel, but historians credit Spanish engineer Genaro Palacios. The Eiffel link is a myth. Source: NHCP; National Museum of the Philippines.

q: Where were the steel parts of San Sebastián Church made?
n: The steel parts of San Sebastián Church were fabricated in Belgium (Binche) and shipped to Manila in the late 1880s. Source: NHCP; National Museum of the Philippines.

q: Which hotel was the first in Asia to be equipped with electric elevators?
n: The Manila Hotel (1912, by William Parsons) was the first hotel in Asia equipped with electric elevators. Source: Manila Hotel official history; NHCP.

q: Which is the first all-steel church in Asia?
n: San Sebastián Church in Quiapo (1891) is the first all-steel church in Asia. Source: NHCP; National Museum of the Philippines.

q: Which Felipe Mendoza building was completed in 1978?
n: Felipe Mendoza's Batasang Pambansa Complex in Quezon City was completed in 1978. Source: House of Representatives history; UAP records.

q: Which of these buildings is not a work of Felipe Mendoza?
n: Quiapo Church is by Juan Nakpil (1933 rebuild). The Batasang Pambansa, Philippine Veterans Bank and LDS church buildings are Felipe Mendoza's. Source: NCCA (Nakpil); UAP Likha Award records (Mendoza).

q: When was the Manila Central Post Office by Juan Arellano completed?
n: Juan Arellano's Neoclassical Manila Central Post Office was completed in 1926. It was rebuilt after its destruction in 1945. Source: NHCP; National Museum (Important Cultural Property).

q: When was Mañosa's Coconut Palace built?
n: Mañosa's Coconut Palace (Tahanang Pilipino) on the CCP Complex was built in 1978. It was offered as a residence for Pope John Paul II's 1981 visit, which he declined. Source: NCCA (Mañosa); Coconut Palace history.

q: What particular church was Architect Jose Maria Zaragoza involved in?
o: Shrine of Nuestra Sefiora de Manaoag
n: José María Zaragoza designed the 1984 expansion of Quiapo Church (Minor Basilica of the Black Nazarene), enlarging the nave to hold the crowds. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Zaragoza); Quiapo Church history.

q: Where is the tallest building in the Philippines?
n: The tallest buildings in the Philippines are in Metro Manila, in Makati and Bonifacio Global City (Taguig). Source: CTBUH Skyscraper Center (Philippines).

q: What is the style of the Manila Metropolitan Theater?
n: The Manila Metropolitan Theater (1931), by Juan Arellano, is Art Deco with Philippine motifs. Source: NHCP; National Commission for Culture and the Arts (MET).

q: Which of the following is not a work of Jose Siao Ling?
n: Jose Siao Ling designed National University buildings (Manila, Laguna, Dentistry). The SM Mall of Asia Arena is not his work. Source: Jose Siao Ling and Associates project list; SM Prime.

q: Which is the first recognized architecture school in the Philippines?
n: Mapúa Institute of Technology (founded 1925 by Tomás Mapúa) is recognized as the first school of architecture in the Philippines. Source: Mapúa University history.

q: Which mixed-use skyscraper in Makati was designed by Gabriel Formoso, is known as the tallest steel-framed building in the Philippines, and was once the tallest building in Makati?
n: Gabriel Formoso designed the Rufino Pacific Tower in Makati (2001), long Makati's tallest building and noted as the tallest steel-framed building in the Philippines. Source: CTBUH Skyscraper Center; Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: Which Juan Arellano building is neoclassical with a grand curved central bay?
n: Juan Arellano's Manila Central Post Office is Neoclassical, with an Ionic colonnade and curved end bays. Source: NHCP; National Museum (Important Cultural Property).

q: Which pre-colonial structure was a royal house of the Maranao?
n: The torogan is the ancestral royal house of the Maranao datu, raised on posts with carved panolong beams. Source: Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino; NCCA.

q: Which people are traditionally linked to the Banaue Rice Terraces?
n: The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved by the Ifugao people and are part of the UNESCO Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras. Source: UNESCO (Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras).

q: In the bahay na bato, what ground-floor space held the carriage?
n: In the bahay na bato, the zaguán is the ground-floor entrance hall where carriages were kept. The azotea is the open terrace. Source: Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino; Zialcita & Tinio, Philippine Ancestral Houses.

q: Which Philippine site was inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List in 1995?
o: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras
n: The Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1995. Source: UNESCO (Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras).

q: Manila Cathedral and which other church were among the seven churches established inside the walled city of Intramuros?
n: Manila Cathedral and San Agustin Church were among the seven churches inside Intramuros, and the only ones to survive World War II. Source: Intramuros Administration.

q: What style is San Sebastián Church?
n: San Sebastián Church is Neo-Gothic (Gothic Revival), built from prefabricated steel. Source: NHCP; National Museum of the Philippines.
